Fulfillment: One champion fights in place of the whole army, and his victory becomes his people's victory: the shepherd boy faces the giant in the LORD's name, fells him with a stone from a sling, and the Philistine army flees. So Jesus fights as our representative champion, destroying the devil and death in His own death and resurrection, that His people may share His victory.
Explanation: TRADITIONAL reading: this row is the single battle, not the man — David himself is already covered by the live 'King David' entry, which does not cite 1 Samuel 17. The representative shape is the point: Goliath demands a champion to decide the fate of both sides (1 Samuel 17:8-10, 16), Israel is dismayed, and one man stands in their place. The New Testament never calls this battle a type, so the parallel is stated as traditional.
